newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia defends curbs on property loans.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia defends curbs on property loans.

text.p: Indonesia's central bank governor Sudradjad Djiwandono said on Wednesday a curb on property loans was needed because a policy of moral suasion had not been effective enough.

The central bank announced on Monday that commercial banks were not allowed to allocate new loans to property developers for land procurement and development, except for construction of low-cost housing.
"A policy of moral suasion was not effective enough to reduce rapid rises in property loans. Therefore, on July 7, we decided to stop loans for land procurement and development," Djiwandono said.
Economists welcomed the ruling as a good preventive move.
Djiwandono said, however, more than 90 percent of loans to the property sector were still classified as without problems.
"Compared with total loan collectivity, the state of property loans is still better," Djiwandono said.
The governor said a fast increase in property loans could endanger monetary stability and the health of the banking sector because of its sensitivity to economic changes.
"...their financing is long-term while banking funds are short-term. Liquidity and market risks faced by banks providing those loans are relatively high," Djiwandono said.
He said property loans as a percentage of total credits rose to 19.61 percent in April 1997 from 12.2 percent in December 1992, with commercial banks posting the highest growth.
